overlaps.title: Duplicated study-ingest transaction skeleton
overlaps.description: Both routes independently implement: file-signature validation -> storage save -> prisma.$transaction(create ImagingStudy, create ImagingImage, conditionally advance a linked ImagingRequest to 'received') -> rollback-delete-file on failure -> audit log. The bridge path adds ingestKey recomputation/dedup/P2002-race handling and an agent status touch; the manual path adds request-driven patient/appointment/case link resolution. No shared 'ingest a study' function exists for either to call.
overlaps.riskIfUnaddressed: A future business-rule change to study creation (e.g. a new required field, a new audit event, a new KVKK constraint) must be applied twice by hand; the two paths have already diverged in minor ways (error-message wording, whether patientId-name-matching is attempted) that a shared function would prevent.

overlaps.title: Update-policy computed two different ways
overlaps.description: bootstrap returns a literal { channel: 'stable', mandatory: false } instead of calling the same bridgeUpdateConfig.ts the dedicated update endpoint uses.
overlaps.riskIfUnaddressed: If the update subsystem's mode/channel defaults ever change, bootstrap's hardcoded stub silently drifts out of sync with the real policy.

overlaps.title: BRG's public HTTP surface is split across two route files by caller identity, not by domain
overlaps.description: This is a deliberate, documented split (admin/clinic-staff endpoints vs device-agent endpoints) rather than an accident, but it means neither file is 'the BRG module' - a reader looking for BRG's full surface must read both, and the file named for the boundary ('imagingBridgePublic.ts') only covers the device-facing half.

overlaps.title: "public" naming collision
overlaps.description: 'Public' in the existing filename means 'reachable before user-session authentication, mounted under /api/public' - an HTTP-trust-boundary sense. The program's own target module shape (per F2-PREP-001/005) uses 'public' to mean 'application-layer public contract surface for other domains to call.' These are different concepts sharing one word; a future module-boundary public.ts contract file would collide in name/intent with the existing route file.

missingPublicSurfaces.gap: No public.ts/contract module exists. F2-PREP-005 §10 already records this: IMG's only 'public contract candidate' is a proposed, not-yet-implemented ImagingStudyReceived event, plus a forward-looking ImagingLifecyclePort/AttachmentLifecyclePort for Privacy's cross-domain writes (F2-PREP-002 F2-CC-14). Every current cross-domain consumer of Imaging (Privacy's 3 services) reaches prisma.imagingImage directly.
missingPublicSurfaces.evidence: grep confirmed zero prisma.imagingImage callers going through any services/imaging/ export; grep confirmed no public.ts/facade.ts/contract.ts file under services/imaging/ or routes/.

missingPublicSurfaces.gap: No dedicated authentication/adapter module for authenticateBridgeAgent() - the entire device-trust boundary (hash lookup, revoked/pending checks, uniform 401) lives inline in routes/imagingBridgePublic.ts with no importable, independently testable module.
No shared 'ingest a study' application service (see OVL-01) - the closest thing to a BRG/IMG public contract today is duplicated inline logic, not a named function either side calls.

findings.summary: routes/imaging.ts's name does not match its actual responsibility: 8 of its 27 routes (30%) manage BRG-owned models (ImagingBridgeAgent, ImagingBridgePairing) with zero ImagingDevice/Request/Study/Image access.
imagingBridgePublic.ts is correctly named for its own content (100% BRG, all device-facing) but does not represent BRG's full surface - the admin half lives elsewhere (OVL-03).
Study/image ingest business logic is duplicated, not shared, between the manual and bridge upload paths (OVL-01).
findings.evidence: server/src/routes/imaging.ts:614-656 vs server/src/routes/imagingBridgePublic.ts:301-341, both read directly in this task.

findings.summary: releaseMetadataValidation.ts contains zero imaging-specific logic and is a generic release-descriptor parser nested inside services/imaging/ purely because its only two current consumers happen to be BRG files.
The only genuinely IMG+BRG shared service file (imagingUploadValidation.ts) is explicit and well-documented about the sharing in its own header - this is a positive finding, not a gap.

Cross-domain direct Prisma access into ImagingImage from three Privacy-domain services is real and independently reconfirmed by this task (not merely cited from F2-PREP-002), and is bounded/documented KVKK-lifecycle behavior (redaction, anonymization, deletion review) rather than an accidental violation - but it means IMG has no enforced facade today.
findings.evidence: grep + direct read of clinicBulkExportConfig.ts, deletionReviewInventory.ts, orphanFileInspection.ts, patientAnonymization.ts.

findings.summary: ImagingBridgePairingDevice has no clinicId/organizationId column, independently reconfirmed by direct schema read (matches F2-PREP-004's prior finding).

windows-bridge-pr.yml's path filter includes server/src/services/imaging/** and server/src/tests/imaging*.ts, but its job step only runs test:imaging, test:imaging-bridge-pairing, test:imaging-bridge-onboarding, and test:imaging-bridge-update - NOT test:kvkk-lifecycle, even though kvkkAttachmentImagingLifecycle.test.ts exercises ImagingStudy/ImagingImage legal-hold and would be affected by a services/imaging/** change. This is a CI-coverage gap, not corrected by this task.

redactStudyLegalHoldReason is an exported (de-facto public) KVKK-relevant symbol with no home outside a route file - it is not in any services/imaging/ module and has no test file of its own beyond imaging.test.ts's route-level assertions.

BRG's device-facing half (imagingBridgePublic.ts) is a textbook anti-corruption/adapter layer by its own explicit header-comment design constraints (no PHI/token/filename logging, uniform 401 on every rejection reason, no storage URL ever returned, content-addressed idempotency independent of agent identity); BRG's admin-facing half (embedded in imaging.ts) is ordinary same-process application logic with no comparable adapter framing. A single 'is BRG an ACL, adapter, or part of IMG' answer is therefore inaccurate - the honest classification is a split: ACL/adapter at the external (device) edge, ordinary domain logic at the internal (admin) edge, both operating on the same 4 BRG-owned models.

brgRoleClassification.rationale: See finding F-10. BRG is neither cleanly 'part of IMG' (it owns 4 distinct Prisma models, a distinct job, distinct tests, and a distinct external deployable) nor cleanly a pure ACL/adapter (its admin-management half is ordinary CRUD indistinguishable in style from IMG's own routes, and it directly writes IMG-owned models during ingest, PUB-RT-02). This task does not resolve the split further; F2-PREP-006-E and/or the eventual pilot-contract task must decide whether to formalize the two edges as distinct sub-modules (e.g. BRG-Admin and BRG-Device) or keep BRG as one module with two entry surfaces.

This task does not authorize, schedule, or recommend a timeline for any file move, module creation, dependency-cruiser rule, or contract implementation - all such items are proposals for F2-PREP-006-E and/or a future, separately-authorized implementation task.

Route responsibility descriptions are derived from HTTP method+path+imports+the surrounding role-array/header-comment context; not every one of the 32 route handler bodies was read line-by-line (the two upload/ingest routes, the pair/bootstrap/update routes, and all local helper functions were read in full; the remaining CRUD-shaped routes were not, since their behavior is fully determined by their path/model/role-array and reading them in full would not change any ownership or overlap conclusion).
